title: Microsoft Entra ID: users, groups and administrative units

videos.script: Every Azure tenant is a directory. It was there before any subscription, and it holds every identity the company has. {{directory}} Its name today is Microsoft Entra ID. Until 2023 it was Azure Active Directory, and many pages still say so. {{name}} Part of it answers anybody. You will ask it where a tenant signs people in, and it will tell you. {{discovery}} Ask about a tenant that does not exist, and it refuses, with an error code of its own. {{refusal}} Inside the directory live users. A user has a name she types, and an id that never changes. Keep the id. {{object}} Users go into groups, and access goes to groups, never to people. Then leaving a group is leaving the access. {{groups}} A dynamic group goes further. A rule over the users' own details decides who is in it, and keeps it current. {{dynamic}} And an administrative unit cuts the directory into slices. A store manager can reset passwords in her slice, and nowhere else. {{unit}} You will write all of it in Terraform, with the provider for Entra ID, and see how far your lab can check it. {{end}}
